definition: A model architecture that jointly encodes a pair of inputs (such as a query and a candidate document) together, allowing rich interaction between them for scoring relevance.
details: Cross-encoders typically achieve higher accuracy than bi-encoders for tasks like re-ranking search results, at the cost of being much slower since each query-document pair must be processed together rather than compared via precomputed embeddings.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Boil it down and it is this: A model architecture that jointly encodes a pair of inputs (such as a query and a candidate document) together, allowing rich interaction between them for scoring relevance. Here is why it matters: Cross-encoders typically achieve higher accuracy than bi-encoders for tasks like re-ranking search results, at the cost of being much slower since each query-document pair must be processed together rather than compared via precomputed embeddings. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is Cross-Encoder.
